messages.content: Can you provide me with the fastest route from my home in San Francisco to my office in Palo Alto and then a scenic route from Palo Alto to the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco, and finally the fastest route back to my home from the Golden Gate Bridge?

function.name: get_directions
function.description: Retrieve directions from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_location.description: The starting point of the journey.

end_location.description: The destination point of the journey.

route_type.description: Type of route to use (e.g., fastest, scenic). Default is fastest.

We need to call get_directions twice: first SF home to Palo Alto fastest, second Palo Alto to Golden Gate scenic. The third leg is Golden Gate to SF home fastest; we can compute that as a separate function call or combine? The function get_directions only supports start_location, end_location, route_type. We can call it twice: first for SF home to Palo Alto fastest, second for Palo Alto to Golden Gate scenic. Then we can compute Golden Gate to SF home fastest separately. But we can also call get_directions for Golden Gate to SF home fastest. So we need three calls. The user wants all three routes. We can call get_directions for each leg. The user didn't specify route_type for the last leg, but we can default to fastest. So we need to call get_directions for SF home to Palo Alto fastest, Palo Alto to Golden Gate scenic, Golden Gate to SF home fastest. We'll do them sequentially.
